name: INAES compliance desk for small co-operatives and mutuales (monthly web filing, CRS identification, member roll, assembly documents)
buyer: Mutuales that run the ayuda economica (lending) service, plus small cooperatives and mutuales that must file assembly documents, accounts and the roll of members and authorities
trigger: INAES Res 1279/2026: monthly regime reported by web transmission within 20 business days of month end, from the July 2026 period, arrears must also use the new system, replacing spreadsheet upload; Res 1038/2026 (26 May 2026) member identification for automatic exchange of financial account information; Res 1687/2026 30-day cure period for lending mutuales; Res 756/2025 and 2147/2025 member and authorities roll; Res 878-879/2024 and 3208/2024 sumarios and suspensions of non-filers.
existing: INAES provides its own web transmission (free). Competitor search 'mutuales ayuda economica regimen informativo INAES software gestion mutual' returned no software vendors, so mutual management software was not confirmed either way.
unchecked: Count of active cooperatives and mutuales and how many are tiny; whether existing mutual management ERPs already export the INAES files; provincial bodies (local competent authority) also receive the filing; UIF obligations of mutuales and cooperatives not checked; willingness to pay by volunteer-run boards.

first_check.duty: Real and in force. INAES Res 1279/2026 was signed on 23-06-2026 and published in the Boletin Oficial No. 35937 on 25-06-2026. It applies to mutuales under the monthly regime of Res 1418/03 art. 17(b) (text ordered by Res 3034/2024). Each month, within 20 business days of month end, they must report compliance with arts. 5, 6, 9 and 10 (Annexes I-V and VII) to INAES and to the local provincial authority. It applies from the July 2026 period, and overdue periods must also be filed through the new system. The resolution itself sets no penalty. Enforcement comes from other rules: Res 1687/2026 gave lending mutuales 30 days to cure missing filings, and Res 878/879/2024 ordered sumarios against thousands of non-compliant entities (secondary sources). Separately, Res 756/2025 requires all co-operatives and mutuales to file a member and authorities roll every year, and quarterly if they are UIF 99/2023 obligated parties (deadline extended by Res 2147/2025). Lending mutuales are UIF obligated parties.
first_check.market: No current national count was found. An older Mercado article cites about 32,000 registered co-operatives and mutuales, but the figure is undated and the register has since been purged; INAES suspended 20,612 co-operatives and 1,847 mutuales in 2019. In 2020 Santa Fe had 850 mutuales, of which 300 offered ayuda economica. The lending-mutual segment that carries the monthly duty is probably around 1,000 to 2,000 nationally, but this is an extrapolation and unverified.
first_check.competitor: The filing itself goes through INAES's own free web system. According to the resolution text, it completely replaces the spreadsheet download and upload flow. It offers manual web entry with validations, autocomplete and partial save, and issues a PDF receipt. No file import or API was found. That means a third-party tool cannot simply generate a file to upload; it would need assisted entry or browser automation, which makes an MVP harder. Mutual management ERPs exist: Grupo Neo Sistemas (NeoConsultores S.A.) sells an integral system for mutuales, with the MutualOnline app. Whether any ERP prepares the INAES annex data was not confirmed. A generic member tool, Gestion Socios, has no INAES features. No vendor was found that specifically offers INAES filing for mutuales.
first_check.reason: The duty is real, monthly and newly changed: from July 2026 the new INAES web system replaces the old spreadsheets and is manual entry only, and overdue periods must be re-entered there. That creates fresh pain for lending mutuales. However, the filing channel is free, the reachable segment is small (probably low thousands of lending mutuales), and the mid-size ones likely already run mutual ERPs such as Neo Sistemas, which may add INAES support. Because there is no import path, a third-party tool would depend on browser automation, which is brittle. Many entities have volunteer boards, so willingness to pay is doubtful. Distribution through accountants and provincial federations is plausible. The yearly or quarterly member roll adds some recurring value.

challenge_check.killer: None found. The partial threats are INAES's own free web transmission system (Res 1279/2026), accountants who already serve mutuales, and the chance that mutual ERPs such as Grupo Neo Sistemas add the INAES annexes.
challenge_check.reason: Nothing kills it. Spanish searches found no vendor that files the INAES ayuda economica return or the nomina for mutuales. The only mutual ERP found was Grupo Neo Sistemas (MutualOnline app), and no INAES export was confirmed for it. INAES Res 1567/2026 (published 3 Aug 2026) adds another recurring duty on the same web system: an AML module with annual sworn statements, a quarterly statistical ROS report and an initial filing within 90 days. That widens the bundle. The weaknesses stay: filing goes through INAES's free web entry, with no import or API found. Accountants and the Consejo Profesional advisory desk already serve these entities. The number of active lending mutuales was not found. The buyers are volunteer boards, and the work is mostly data entry, not a tool gap.
